hypotheses.statement: Increasing implementation capacity causes no binding-bottleneck migration.
Implementation remains the dominant binding bottleneck under higher capacity.
All workflow stages accelerate proportionally, so relative constraints do not migrate.
Any apparent migration is caused by measurement or instrumentation overhead.
Any apparent migration is caused by task difficulty or task mix.
Migration is domain- or repository-specific rather than general across the bounded cohort.
Any apparent migration is caused by validation or harness artifacts.
Environment readiness or availability, not workflow constraint, causes apparent migration.
Candidate multiplicity increases coordination, selection, or review load enough to offset implementation gains.
Under higher implementation capacity, at least one non-implementation stage becomes a binding throughput constraint while implementation ceases to be binding.

logical_note: H0 is the null; H1-H8 are retained rival mechanisms and can overlap. HM is the target hypothesis. No hypothesis has been evaluated.
